answers.children: Skye Terriers are moderately good with children when the children are gentle. Their small size and low-slung build make them vulnerable to rough play that can tug their long double coat, while their courageous independent nature leads them to snap rather than retreat if tolerance wears thin. The breed’s history of facing down larger animals reinforces this bold streak around energetic toddlers. (PawLabs child-friendly score: 5/10)
answers.other-pets: Skye Terriers do not always get along with other pets. Bred on the Isle of Skye to hunt vermin and small game such as foxes and badgers, they retain a strong prey drive that makes small animals risky companions, and their stubborn loyalty often favours one person over sharing attention with fellow dogs.
answers.exercise: Skye Terriers need two 30-minute walks daily. Their moderate energy and short-legged build suit steady neighbourhood sniffing rather than long hikes; when this level is not met the independent terrier becomes bored, tears up flower beds or barks persistently at imaginary quarry.
answers.shedding: Yes, Skye Terriers shed moderately year-round. Their long double coat with flowing hair traps loose undercoat and mats easily behind the ears and on the belly, so daily brushing is required to stop the elegant feathering from spreading hair across furniture despite the moderate shedding score.
answers.hypoallergenic: No breed is hypoallergenic and the Skye Terrier is not one commonly suggested for allergy sufferers. The long double coat typical of this Scottish breed continues to produce dander and loose hair that can trigger reactions, while the high grooming demands of its flowing texture add to household allergen buildup.
answers.training: Skye Terriers are not easy to train. Their intelligence is paired with stubborn independence bred into them for hunting vermin without constant direction, so they learn commands on their own terms and can appear aloof during sessions, demanding patient consistency from owners rather than quick biddability.
answers.lifespan: Skye Terriers live 12-14 years. Their small yet sturdy low-slung build from the rugged Isle of Skye supports reasonable health robustness, and the breed’s history as both tenacious hunters and elite companions shows they can maintain condition when their moderate energy and grooming needs are met consistently.
answers.size: Skye Terriers reach 25-40 lb and stand 9-10 in at the shoulder. This compact yet substantial build with a long body and short legs gives them a low centre of gravity that feels surprisingly solid for their height, allowing the courageous terrier to stand its ground despite the small stature.
answers.barking: Skye Terriers bark moderately. Their courageous nature and history of guarding Highland burrows against larger foes prompt sharp alerts at strangers or unusual sounds, while the independent streak can lead to persistent barking during long owner absences if boredom sets in.
answers.apartment: Skye Terriers can live in an apartment. Their small size, moderate energy satisfied by short walks and ability to lounge independently indoors suit compact homes, provided the high grooming demands of the long coat and tendency to bark at strangers are managed so noise does not disturb neighbours.
answers.first-time: Skye Terriers are not a good first dog. The high grooming demands of their long double coat combined with stubborn independence and aloofness toward strangers require experienced handling, patience and respect for the breed’s loyal yet courageous terrier character that does not readily yield to novice owners.
